clue.text: A cleaner fuel that draws well

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaning lady
coal is a fuel burnt for heat

explanation.surface: A fuel praised for burning cleanly and keeping a good draught going in the fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws well' suggests a chimney's draught, but it means drawing pictures: artists sketch with sticks of this. A char is a British term for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists use sticks of burnt wood for sketching, so it is a medium that is good for drawing.

clue.text: Has an inherent desire for animals

indicators.note: inherent means existing within, so the desire word sits inside the word has

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have a built-in longing for creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: These scavenging African carnivores are examples of animals.

parts.note: a chicken run contains a perching pole where hens settle at night

explanation.surface: A Polish fugitive escaping the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish person and 'on the run' as fleeing, but the pole is a perch inside a hen run.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds rest for the night is a pole of this kind.

clue.text: Unbridled carthorse needs one with a stick to start

definitions.text: Unbridled carthorse needs one with a stick to start

indicators.note: unbridled means running wild, so the letters of carthorse are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A runaway cart horse needs someone with a whip to get it going.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'one with a stick' looks like a driver with a whip, but in the whole-clue reading it is the conductor with a baton, needed before musicians can begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony ensemble waits for its conductor's baton before playing, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Pays a brief visit to watch over transgression

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: to look is to watch
a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop by briefly on someone is an idiom for a short call.

parts.note: the American term for property in land and buildings

explanation.surface: Arriving on American soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a verb, arriving somewhere, but it is the noun: property, using the US word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call real estate by this word, meaning property in land.

indicators.note: carries means holds inside, so the league letter is held within the general word

parts.note: rife means widespread or general
L is an abbreviation for league

explanation.surface: A military general holds a weapon belonging to some league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer, but it is the adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled gun is a firearm, a type of weapon.

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a company is a business

explanation.surface: Instructions to take an invoice along to a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort or attend someone is to go along with them.

clue.text: Oppressive cranny, it needs freshening up

indicators.note: freshening up means rearranging, so the letters of cranny and it are reworked

explanation.surface: A stuffy nook that badly needs airing out.
explanation.definitionFit: A despotic ruler is cruel and harsh, the way an oppressive regime is.

clue.text: Valiant choir somehow held a note

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the note sits within the rearranged choir letters
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of choir are rearranged

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A brave choir managed to sustain a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns CHOIR into HROIC, and 'held' puts E inside it after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and bold, like a valiant hero.

clue.text: They lead in the forces if ordered

definitions.text: They lead in the forces if ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters of forces and if are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Commanders take charge in the armed services when given orders to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' plays on military orders, but signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Commissioned ranks command troops, so the whole clue describes what they do.

parts.note: a woman serving tables writes down what any diner asks for

explanation.surface: A woman who will obey whoever commands her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes orders' suggests obedience, but these are food orders in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman serving in a restaurant notes each customer's choice of meal.

clue.text: I hesitate to claim such valuable fur

parts.note: er is the sound one makes when hesitating
saying mine is how one claims something

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates before laying claim to a precious fur.
explanation.definitionFit: The white winter coat of the stoat is a prized pelt used for royal robes.

parts.note: an idiom for interfering, read literally as taking up a paddle to row a boat

explanation.surface: Someone was drawn into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' as a quarrel, but the literal picture is rowing (rhymes with 'go'): the idiom means to interfere uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to meddle in others' business uninvited, as one does by joining a quarrel.

parts.note: alludes to the saying 'no names, no' followed by this punishment: if no one is named, no one is punished

explanation.surface: Anonymous troops avoid a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'no names, no pack drill' means nobody will be blamed if nobody is named; the punishment was marching in full kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A military punishment of marching while carrying a full kitbag.

parts.note: occupation as living in a property without right, and sedentary as crouched on one's heels

explanation.surface: A desk job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' looks like a job, but it means occupying a building unlawfully; 'Sedentary' hints at a crouching posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Living in an empty building without permission, also a crouching sitting posture.

indicators.note: in places the tea word inside the bag word

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy tea packed in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buy' is a noun here, as in 'a good buy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acquired for money, a buy or acquisition.

parts.note: the traditional seaside puppet couple who beat each other with a stick

explanation.surface: A slapstick double act from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: A traditional British seaside puppet show in which a hook-nosed husband and his wife hit each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional puppet show featuring a quarrelling married pair who trade blows.

clue.text: Lease in legal document taken out

indicators.note: in places the lease word inside the document word

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
to let is to lease

explanation.surface: A lease included in a contract has been removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erased or struck out has been removed.

explanation.surface: Is King Lear the monarch meant here?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's king, but the other sense is the Victorian nonsense poet who shared a first name with several English monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English monarchs bore this name, and so did the nonsense poet who wrote 'The Owl and the Pussycat'.

clue.text: Sharp American intelligence organisation gets backing about detectives

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed agency goes round the detectives
backing means going in reverse, so the agency's initials are turned round

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the USA
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A US spy agency receives support regarding police detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' could be a person's wit, but here it is a sour taste; 'backing' looks like support for the agency, yet it signals reading the initials backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour, tart taste can be called sharp.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
to lean is to incline

explanation.surface: Lots of people tend to be immaculate.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of dirt or stains, immaculate.

clue.text: A certain laxity allowed in angular measurement

explanation.surface: Some leeway permitted when measuring angles.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom of action or leeway; also the angular distance north or south of the equator.

clue.text: Painful reminder of passion when taken to heart

definitions.text: Painful reminder of passion when taken to heart

parts.words: Painful reminder of passion when taken to heart
parts.note: a painful pulsing, which placed after the word heart makes an object of passion

explanation.surface: A love affair leaves an aching memory.
explanation.walkthrough: A pulsing ache is a painful reminder; add it to 'heart' and you get a heart-throb, someone adored.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhythmic aching pulse, which joined to heart names an idol of passion.

indicators.note: somehow means in some way, so the letters of fit and names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to squeeze names into a list one way or another.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's cargo or passenger list is called by this word.

clue.text: An encroachment on the public highway?

parts.note: on can mean in, as in on the scene or in it
a road is a public highway

explanation.surface: Trespassing onto a public road.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance into territory belonging to someone else is an incursion or encroachment.

explanation.surface: A great composer of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like an adjective meaning excellent, but it is a capital city; the songwriter is Irving Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany's capital city, and the surname of composer Irving, who wrote 'White Christmas'.

explanation.surface: A servant working at a graveyard for animals.
explanation.walkthrough: A British term for a drudge who does menial jobs; the second reading is literally a hound's corpse, found in a pet cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge who does the menial jobs; read literally, a hound's corpse, as buried in a pet graveyard.
